newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta says Timor shadow government plan bizarre.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta says Timor shadow government plan bizarre.

text.p: Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas has dismissed as "risky and bizarre" a plan by East Timor resistance leader Jose Ramos Horta to form a shadow government, the official Antara news agency reported on Thursday.

"Apparently, Ramos Horta has run out of ideas to attract the sympathy of the international community. Now he has to resort to the more risky and bizarre ways," Alatas was quoted as saying on Wednesday.
Nobel Peace laureate Ramos Horta said last month that up to two thirds of the so-called shadow government would be made up of activists in hiding in East Timor.
He said some members of the group had already been selected with the endorsement of resistance leader Xanana Gusmao, who is serving a 20-year jail term in Jakarta for subversion.
Antara said some local Timorese figures included on Ramos Horta's list said they had no knowledge of the plan.

"I don't know exactly about it. I am even shocked when finding my name on the list of Horta's newly-formed shadow government in the newspaper," Armindo Maia, rector of East Timor University, was quoted as saying.
Indonesia invaded the former Portuguese colony of East Timor in 1975 and annexed it a year later in a move not recognised by the United Nations.
Ramos Horta, who lives in Australia, was jointly awarded the 1996 Nobel Peace Prize with East Timor Roman Catholic Bishop Carlos Belo.
